project.description: Seven-year master plan expansion of the Cyril Z. Meadow Institute's graduate psychoanalytic training facility: porch roof, ramp and fire door on the existing barn, conversion of a shed to a clinical studies lab, a new separate residential building housing faculty bedrooms, lounges and a kitchen (described on the site plan form as an apartment), sewer and water upgrades, new parking, and increased class size, hours and events. Site plan approval is at issue in this docket.

judgments.note: Municipal appeal is clear. Housing hinges on whether the new 'residential building to house faculty bedrooms, student and faculty lounges, and a kitchen' for a psychoanalytic institute is new housing (a residence) or institutional lodging akin to a dormitory/inn; the site plan form says 'apartment' but no dwelling units are described. Left housing unknown, so uncertain.
See disposition; the primary use is a nonresidential educational facility, but a new residential building is part of the proposal.
The court states appellants are entitled to have the application considered on its merits de novo in the present appeals, with a merits hearing scheduled.
Filing date not stated; the only dated event is the 2004-08-13 decision, which leaves a zero-day minimum, so kind and days are unknown.
The residential building's number of dwelling units (if any) is not stated.
No subdivision is mentioned, but the documents do not state that none is proposed.

The decided issues (preclusion, deemed approval) are legal; the merits contentions on site plan standards are not described, and the character-of-the-area argument is aimed at prior permit conditions generally, not shown as a site plan contention in this docket.
